steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' library.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have the necessary imports to start building a React component with state.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState, which are essential for building components with state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import React and useState from 'react' to proceed.

steps.title: Create the SearchComponent function component
steps.instruction: Create a function component named SearchComponent that returns null initially.
steps.hint: Define a function called SearchComponent that returns null. You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create SearchComponent function component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named SearchComponent is defined and returns null.
successCriteria: SearchComponent is defined as a function and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the SearchComponent function component. This establishes the foundation for our search UI.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've defined a function named SearchComponent that returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've created a function component named SearchComponent that returns null.

steps.title: Initialize search query state
steps.instruction: Inside the SearchComponent function, use the useState hook to create a state variable named 'searchQuery' with an initial value of an empty string.
steps.hint: Call useState with an empty string as the initial value, and destructure the returned array to get the state variable and setter function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating a state variable for user input
const [username, setUsername] = useState('');
steps.expectedOutcome: The SearchComponent function will have a searchQuery state variable initialized to an empty string, ready to store user input.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called with an empty string, and the returned array is destructured into 'searchQuery' and 'setSearchQuery'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the searchQuery state. This variable will hold the user's search input as they type.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using useState with an empty string initial value and destructuring it into 'searchQuery' and 'setSearchQuery'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Inside the SearchComponent function, use useState to create a state variable named 'searchQuery' starting with an empty string value.

steps.title: Initialize search results state
steps.instruction: Inside the SearchComponent function, add another useState hook to create a state variable called 'searchResults' initialized with an empty array.
steps.hint: Follow the same pattern as the searchQuery state, but name the variable 'searchResults' and set its initial value to [].
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: state for a list of items
const [items, setItems] = useState([]);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have two state variables: searchQuery (string) and searchResults (array).
successCriteria: A state variable named 'searchResults' is declared with useState, initialized to an empty array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added state to track search results. This array will hold the data we fetch later.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with the exact variable name 'searchResults' and initializing it to [].
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Add 'const [searchResults, setSearchResults] = useState([]);' inside the component function.

steps.title: Create handleSearchInputChange handler
steps.instruction: Inside your SearchComponent, create a function named handleSearchInputChange that takes an event parameter and updates the searchQuery state with the input's current value.
steps.hint: Define a function that calls setSearchQuery with event.target.value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleSearchInputChange function is defined that updates searchQuery when called with an input event.
successCriteria: The handleSearchInputChange function is defined, takes an event parameter, and calls setSearchQuery with event.target.value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the input change handler that will update the search query state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it takes an event parameter and calls setSearchQuery with event.target.value.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try creating a function named handleSearchInputChange that updates the searchQuery state with the input value from an event.

steps.title: Return basic component structure with search input
steps.instruction: Return JSX from your component with a search input field. The input should have its value bound to the searchQuery state and its onChange event wired to the handleSearchInputChange handler.
steps.hint: Replace the current return statement with JSX containing an input element. Use the value and onChange attributes to connect it to your state and handler.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a search input field that displays the current searchQuery value and updates it when the user types.
successCriteria: The component returns JSX with an input element that has value={searchQuery} and onChange={handleSearchInputChange}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the search input field and connected it to your state and handler.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your input element has both the value and onChange attributes correctly set.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component doesn't return the expected JSX structure with a properly connected input field.

steps.title: Add search button to the UI
steps.instruction: Add a button element after the input in your component's return statement to trigger searches.
steps.hint: Place a <button> element right after the closing tag of the <input>. You can give it text like 'Search'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will now show a search button next to the input field.
successCriteria: A <button> element is added after the <input> element in the return statement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added a search button to the UI.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added a <button> element after the input.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button wasn't added correctly. Check that you placed a <button> element in the return statement after the input.

steps.title: Create mock search API function
steps.instruction: Create a mockSearchAPI function that simulates an API call with a delay and returns search results as a promise. Place it inside your SearchComponent function, above the return statement.
steps.hint: Define a function that returns a new Promise. Inside the promise, use setTimeout to simulate network delay, then resolve with mock data.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a mockSearchAPI function that returns a promise with simulated delay, ready to be called later.
successCriteria: The mockSearchAPI function is defined, returns a Promise, uses setTimeout to simulate delay, and resolves with mock search results.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a mock API function that simulates network delay.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function returns a Promise and uses setTimeout to delay the response.
steps.feedbackWrong: The mockSearchAPI function isn't quite right. It should return a Promise that resolves with mock data after a delay.

steps.title: Create handleSearchSubmit handler
steps.instruction: Create a function named handleSearchSubmit inside your component. This function should call the mockSearchAPI function with the current searchQuery and update the searchResults state with the returned data.
steps.hint: Define a function that uses the mockSearchAPI and setSearchResults to update the results state.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleSearchSubmit function is defined that calls mockSearchAPI and updates searchResults state.
successCriteria: The handleSearchSubmit function is defined, calls mockSearchAPI with searchQuery, and updates searchResults with the returned data.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the handleSearchSubmit handler that will trigger the search and update results.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it calls mockSearchAPI with searchQuery and updates searchResults with the returned data.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleSearchSubmit function is not properly defined. It should call mockSearchAPI and update the searchResults state.

steps.title: Wire search button to handleSearchSubmit
steps.instruction: Add a search button to your component's return statement and wire its onClick handler to call the handleSearchSubmit function.
steps.hint: Add a <button> element with an onClick attribute that calls handleSearchSubmit. Place it after the input element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will display a search button that triggers the search submission when clicked.
successCriteria: A <button> element is added with onClick={handleSearchSubmit}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully wired the search button to trigger the search handler.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it has onClick={handleSearchSubmit} to properly trigger the search.
steps.feedbackWrong: The search button isn't properly connected. Add a <button> with onClick={handleSearchSubmit}.

lessonTitle: Build race condition safe search UI
